install.title: Getting Started
install.html:
Using MCP Servers in this Repository

TypeScript-based servers in this repository can be started with npx.

For example, this will start the Memory server:

npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory

Python-based servers in this repository can be started with uvx or pip. uvx is recommended for ease of use and setup.

For example, this will start the Git server:

# With uvx
uvx mcp-server-git

# With pip
pip install mcp-server-git
python -m mcp_server_git

Follow these instructions to install uv / uvx and these to install pip.

Using an MCP Client

However, running a server on its own isn't very useful, and should instead be configured into an MCP client. For example, here's the Claude Desktop configuration to use the above server:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}

On Windows, wrap npx with cmd /c:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}

Additional examples of using the Claude Desktop as an MCP client might look like:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/allowed/files"]
    },
    "git": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-git", "--repository", "path/to/git/repo"]
    },
    "fetch": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]
    }
  }
}

On Windows, apply the same wrapper to the npx-based filesystem entry above by changing its "command" to "cmd" and prepending "/c", "npx" to its existing args. Leave the uvx entries unchanged.

Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP

An MCP server talks to its client over a transport. The protocol defines two standard ones, and they run very differently:

Transport How the server runs How a client reaches it
stdio The client launches the server as a subprocess and talks to it over the process's stdin and stdout. The server opens no port. A command and args in the client's configuration, as in the examples above
Streamable HTTP The server runs on its own as an HTTP service, and can serve many clients A URL, such as http://localhost:3001/mcp

Every server in this repository serves stdio by default, and every one can also serve Streamable HTTP on http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp (set PORT and HOST to move it): Everything with its streamableHttp argument (its README also covers its deprecated HTTP+SSE transport), and the others with --transport streamable-http, as each server's README shows. Started without one, a server uses stdio, so when you run uvx mcp-server-git or npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory in a terminal, it opens no port, prints at most a one-line startup notice, and then appears to hang. That is expected: it is waiting for a client to send it messages on stdin. You do not normally start a stdio server yourself; your MCP client starts it from its configuration and stops it when it is done.

To try a server without setting up a client, use the MCP Inspector. Given a stdio server's command, it launches the server for you and lets you browse and call its tools; given a URL, it connects to a running Streamable HTTP server:

# A stdio server: the Inspector launches it
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector uvx mcp-server-git

# A Streamable HTTP server: start it first, then connect to its URL
npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything streamableHttp   # or: uvx mcp-server-time --transport streamable-http
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --transport http --server-url http://localhost:3001/mcp

For more, see the transport layer in the MCP architecture overview, and Transports in the specification.
